key_insight: The paper shows that homothetic forward self-similar Navier–Stokes solutions are highly constrained: they do not exist nontrivially in 3D under regularity assumptions, and in 2D the only decaying case is the Oseen vortex.
engineering_relevance: This sharpens which self-similar flow structures are mathematically admissible, informing stability analysis, turbulence theory, and any singular-limit strategy for studying possible non-uniqueness in incompressible flows.
method: Prove a Liouville theorem for homothetic self-similar Navier–Stokes solutions.
Analyze the 2D decaying case and identify the Oseen vortex as the唯一 admissible solution.
Study the linearized Euler operator around the Oseen vortex to assess stability and detect an unstable approximate eigenvalue in a homothetic example.
evidence_signal: The results are theoretical and are supported by analytical proofs in 2D and 3D, including stability analysis of the linearized Euler operator and an example exhibiting an unstable approximate eigenvalue.
watch_item: The conclusions apply to sufficiently regular initial data and decaying/self-similar settings, so they do not automatically rule out more singular or non-decaying flow scenarios.
paper_title: Homothetic Self-Similar Solutions to the Incompressible Navier-Stokes Equations
